The missing Code and FAQ in the early gift example were concrete obstacles to
further investigation. Later work retained the September 2023 and January 2026
Code editions and located paragraph 3.11 in each. The paragraph states the gift
restriction and its fee-or-charge discount exception
\citep[para.~3.11]{sfccode2023,sfccode2026}. Selecting an edition for a test date
is useful progress. It does not decide every question about when a provision
applies, and the source collection still has unresolved statutory definitions.

The FAQ illustrates the dating problem. Its page is associated
with 30 September 2010, but the retained text says that answers to Questions 2
and 4 were updated on 15 October 2024. That does not establish that Question 1
changed. It does establish that the page cannot be treated as an independently
preserved copy of everything a reviewer would have read in 2010. A historical
use must retain that uncertainty \citep{sfcgiftfaq}.

Question 1 also sharpens the business question. It asks about gifts used to
promote a product category. Its answer brings gifts linked to certain types of
funds or funds from particular fund houses within the requirement
\citep[Question 1, answer and section reference]{sfcgiftfaq}. That helps establish
why a product-type link matters. It does not remove the discount exception from
the Code. For a proposed fee rebate, the reviewer must still determine whether
the benefit falls within that exception. ``This requirement applies'' and
``this benefit is prohibited'' answer different questions.

The later development work also examined the SFC circular on the shortening of
US securities settlement to one business day after trading. A cash calculation
alone cannot express its requirements. The circular asks licensed corporations
to consider liquidity, staffing and training, operational processes, technology
and communication with affected clients. It separately addresses management
companies of authorized funds \citep{sfctplusone2024}. A rule about staff
availability and a rule about funding may both be necessary, while neither
covers the communication duty.
